newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X rises after CEO enthusiasm.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X rises after CEO enthusiasm.

text.p: Trading in Bre-X Minerals Ltd was fast and furious again on Friday morning, as investors seemed to gain some confidence about a proposed agreement between Bre-X and Barrick Gold Corp.
Bre-X shares were up C$0.65 to C$21.55 with 1.4 million shares trading hands in the first couple hours of trading on Friday.

The stock started its climb late in the day on Thursday, rising C$1.30 after comments from Bre-X chief executive David Walsh enthused investors, analysts said. Walsh told Reuters that shareholders would not be disappointed with the deal.
"As a result of our negotiating team, we were able to substantially enhance the Barrick offer," he said Thursday. "I think the shareholders will be pleased with the job we've done."
Walsh said the Barrick offer was more attractive than two previous offers to participate in the huge Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.
He would not elaborate, but reiterated his comments Friday morning on Canada's CBC Television's Newsworld, a 24-hour news channel.
The comments prompted a fresh round of rampant rumors about the terms of a deal, analysts said.
"It's all just speculation," said gold analyst Rick Cohen at Goepel Shields in Vancouver. "Based on his (Walsh's) comments, he's pretty excited about it."
The companies have been very tight-lipped about the terms of the proposal, noted gold analyst Egizio Bianchini at Nesbitt Burns.
"We don't know the number. Nobody knows the number," he said.

Barrick Gold's stock had fallen C$0.95 to C$40.15 by midday on Friday, probably because investors believe the company will end up paying more for an interest in Busang than previously thought, analysts said.
The two companies have presented a joint proposal to the Indonesian government and are waiting for a response from government officials.
Most analysts expect the response to come early next week, but the companies have said they did not know when the government would respond.
